questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code uses its thread pool and per-thread connections? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
`resolve_many` is called with 100 ids, of which only 40 are distinct, on a resolver with `max_workers=8`. What is true?
choices: Up to 100 directory lookups run concurrently because each is submitted as a future
40 lookups are submitted; at most 8 run at once and the rest wait in the executor's queue
Duplicates are looked up again, but their results overwrite each other safely
At most 8 lookups are submitted; the others are rejected

questions.prompt: How many directory connections can this resolver hold open at the same time?
choices: Exactly one, shared and reused by all workers
One per worker thread that has handled at least one lookup, so at most max_workers
One per principal id looked up

questions.prompt: The 3-second deadline passes while 2 lookups are still executing in worker threads. Which statement is correct?
choices: Both threads are interrupted and the lookups stop immediately
`resolve_many` waits until both lookups finish, ignoring the deadline
The caller gets those two ids as failures at about the deadline, but the lookups may keep occupying their workers until they finish
The two ids are retried automatically on fresh threads
